hero.title: Camouflage is for prey.
hero.lede: If your company looks and sounds like its competitors, that is the problem we solve. OOVERT is a brand strategy and identity studio: we name companies, decide what they stand for, and design the brand that carries it.

premise.statement: Most branding is camouflage.
premise.body: Safe colours. Borrowed language. A logo built to upset no one, and forgotten by everyone. That is not branding. It is money spent to stay invisible, and companies pay it every month.
premise.counter: We build the opposite.
premise.pullLine: A clear brand is a business asset.
premise.pullNote: It shortens your sales cycle, protects your pricing when the market gets nervous, and gives customers a reason to choose you before they have even spoken to you.

manifesto.text: Visibility is economics. It starts with Strategy, the one true thing no competitor can copy, sharpened by Positioning until the market cannot look away. Then the Logo that seals it, a mark recognised before it is read. The Identity that carries it everywhere: type, colour, voice, one system. Guidelines keep it sharp in every hand that touches it. Camouflage is for prey. We build brands that refuse to hide.

packages.guarantee: Money-back guarantee. If the work is not right, we keep going until it is, or we refund you.

evidence.note: We do not publish a client wall. The numbers that matter in your category, and clients you can call, are yours on request.

studio.statement: Senior hands only. Four disciplines. One question: would we sign it?

principles.text: We show you one direction, not three. Choosing is the hard part, and it is the part you are paying us for.
If something is not working, we say so in the room, not in the wrap-up email.
Good taste is not a line on the invoice. It is the reason to hire a studio like this one.
If the strategy cannot survive being explained in a hallway in one breath, it is not finished.

studio.where: A distributed studio across six timezones. We work wherever the project takes us.

items.q: How can you charge a fraction of the usual agency price?
items.a: Senior people, no overhead, no account managers, no juniors billed as experts. You pay for the work and the taste, not the office. The thinking is the same one a network agency would charge ten times for.

items.q: Do you only design logos, or the whole brand?
items.a: The logo is one part. We name companies, decide what they stand for, and build the whole system the logo lives inside: strategy, voice, colour, type and motion.

items.q: Will our brand end up looking like everyone else's?
items.a: No. Everything is built on the one true thing about your company that no competitor can honestly claim, so the result is specific to you by construction. We do not start from templates or trends. Camouflage is the enemy here: a brand that blends in is a brand that gets missed.

items.q: We already have a brand. Do we start from scratch?
items.a: Rarely. We begin by auditing what you have and finding the equity worth keeping, the recognisable parts you have already paid for in years of recognition. Then we sharpen the positioning and rebuild only what is holding you back. A good rebrand should feel like the company finally looking like itself.
Fixed-scope projects ship in two to five working days. A full strategy-led identity runs a few weeks, because the thinking cannot be rushed. You get a real date before we start.

items.q: What do you need from us to get started?
items.a: A short kickoff, honest access to the people who know the company best, and decisions when we ask for them. We carry the strategy, the making and the detail. Your part is candour and a few well-timed calls, and most of the load stays with us.
Every package lists its rounds, and the recommended tier is unlimited. Either way the money-back guarantee stands: we keep going until you are happy, or we refund you.

items.q: Who owns the final brand and files?
items.a: You do. Full rights and every source file transfer to you on final payment. No licensing games, no holding your logo hostage.

items.q: You are a distributed studio. How do we actually work together?
items.a: Senior people across six timezones, in direct contact with you start to finish. Calls when they matter, async when they do not, and one person who owns your project.

contact.statement: Say it out loud.
contact.note: If you are serious about the work, tell us about the project and roughly what you plan to invest. We read everything that fits.

llmsTxt:
# OOVERT

> OOVERT is a brand strategy and identity studio. We design logos, build brand identities, and write the brand guidelines that keep them sharp. If a company looks and sounds like its competitors, that is the problem we solve.

OOVERT is a distributed studio working across six timezones, founded in 2020. It pairs brand strategy with identity design and staffs projects with senior people only. Tagline: "Camouflage is for prey." Agency-grade branding at a fraction of the usual cost. Professional branding in the US averages about $7,500; OOVERT starts at $280.

## What we do
- Brand strategy: a few weeks of interviews, audits and honest questions to find the one true thing about a company that no competitor can copy.
- Logo design: one mark that compresses the whole company, drawn on a grid so it holds from favicon to facade, delivered in every format.
- Brand identity: logo, type, colour, voice and motion, built into one system people recognise before they finish reading the name.
- Brand guidelines: the rules that keep the identity sharp after handover, written for the people who use them every day.

## Pricing
- One-time projects: Basic ($280), Premium Branding ($480), The Brand Ecosystem ($987).
- Monthly retainer (design on tap; pause or cancel anytime): Solo ($4,999/mo), Studio ($7,999/mo), Scale (custom).
- Staff augmentation (senior people embedded in your team): Dedicated Designer ($3,900/mo), Design Pod ($8,900/mo), Embedded Team (from $18k/mo).
- Every engagement carries a money-back guarantee.

## The studio
Senior hands only, four disciplines. OOVERT shows one considered direction rather than three, says what is not working in the room rather than in a wrap-up email, and treats good taste as the reason to hire a studio like this one. Distributed across six timezones.
